input: Search all .js files under /src for the string 'console.log'. Replace every occurrence with 'logger.info' in-place. Print each modified filename and how many replacements were made per file. At the end, print 'Files modified: N' with the total count of files changed.

transcript.final_response:
I replaced every `console.log` with `logger.info` in the `.js` files under `/src`, editing the files in place.

```
/src/app.js: 1 replacement(s)
/src/index.js: 2 replacement(s)
/src/middleware.js: 2 replacement(s)
Files modified: 3
```

`/src/utils.js` had no occurrences, so it wasn't changed. A search afterwards found no `console.log` left and showed all 5 `logger.info` lines where they should be.

The change only renames the calls. If any of these files doesn't already define or import `logger`, those lines will fail when they run until you add it.
tool_calls:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import os
n=0
for root,_,files in os.walk('/src'):
    for f in sorted(files):
        if not f.endswith('.js'): continue
        p=os.path.join(root,f)
        s=open(p).read()
        c=s.count('console.log')
        if c:
            open(p,'w').write(s.replace('console.log','logger.info'))
            print(f"{p}: {c} replacement(s)")
            n+=1
print(f"Files modified: {n}")
EOF
echo ---; grep -rn 'console.log\|logger.info' /src
